Four households are billed in groups that their signed householding agreements contradict: **HH-0586, HH-0592, HH-0928 and HH-4821**. Each has a signed letter saying all three of its accounts are billed together as one group "from the next billing cycle." As of 15 April 2026, each is still billed as two groups, with the child's individual account kept apart from the parents' joint account and IRA.

| Household | Agreement (signed) | Billing groups in the portfolio system (last changed) |
|---|---|---|
| HH-0586 Quarshie | AGR-0586-3 (2024-06-07): joint account, Saoirse's IRA and Amara's individual account billed as one group | BG-0586-1 = joint + IRA; BG-0586-2 = Amara's account (2021-09-01) |
| HH-0592 Haddad | AGR-0592-3 (2023-10-20): joint account, Bilal's IRA and Fatima's individual account billed as one group | BG-0592-1 = joint + IRA; BG-0592-2 = Fatima's account (2021-09-01) |
| HH-0928 Jablonski | AGR-0928-3 (2024-03-05): joint account, Hugo's IRA and Nikhil's individual account billed as one group | BG-0928-1 = joint + IRA; BG-0928-2 = Nikhil's account (2021-09-01) |
| HH-4821 Lind | AGR-4821-3 (2024-11-18): joint account, Henrik's IRA and Ngozi's individual account billed as one group | BG-4821-1 = joint + IRA; BG-4821-2 = Ngozi's account (2021-09-14) |

**Why these are real discrepancies:**
- In each case the billing groups were last changed on the date the child's own advisory agreement was signed. That was before the householding letter, so the split was never updated after the letter.
- I found nothing in the files that would explain the split: no later change to the agreement, no cancellation and no approved exception.
- Each household's annual review on 2025-10-14 says "No changes requested."
- The custodian's account files show each household holds exactly these three accounts.

**How I searched:** I checked the CRM in all 92 household folders. These four are the only ones with a "householding" agreement. No billing file or other document mentions householding or a billing exception.

**Not counted:** HH-7350 has an advisory agreement stating Aiko "has not agreed to household billing." That is not a householding agreement, so it falls outside your question and I didn't check its billing groups.

**Not done:** I didn't work out how much each household was overbilled. All billing groups use the same tiered fee schedule, which is charged separately per billing group. Combining them could put more assets into lower-rate tiers, but working out the effect would need the quarter-end values.

- "unresolved": the households the files cannot settle, each as {"household_id": ..., "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
